questions.question: Relative humidity is:
options: The vapour actually present expressed as a percentage of the maximum the air could hold AT THAT TEMPERATURE
The mass of vapour in grams per cubic metre
The temperature at which dew forms
The total rainfall for the month

questions.question: Air at 20 °C can hold at most 17 g/m³ of water vapour and actually contains 8,5 g/m³. Its relative humidity is:
That same air is cooled to 10 °C, where the maximum it can hold is about 8,5 g/m³. Its relative humidity is now:
options: 100% — the air is SATURATED; nothing was added, the container simply shrank

questions.question: The dew point is best described as:
options: The temperature at which water boils
The mass of vapour in the air
The percentage of the sky covered by cloud
The temperature to which air must be COOLED for it to become saturated — a moisture measurement disguised as a temperature

subtopics.title: Condensation — From Dew to the Condensation Level

questions.question: Frost rather than dew forms when:
options: The dew point lies BELOW 0 °C, so vapour deposits directly as ice — which is why farmers watch for clear, windless winter nights

questions.question: The fog that rolls into Port Nolloth and the west-coast towns is:
options: Radiation fog from a still valley night
ADVECTION fog — moist maritime air moving horizontally over the cold Benguela Current is chilled below its dew point

questions.question: Adiabatic cooling means a rising parcel of air cools because:
options: It EXPANDS as the surrounding pressure falls — cooling without heat being removed; 1 °C per 100 m when unsaturated, about 0,5 °C per 100 m once saturated

questions.question: Surface temperature 25 °C, surface dew point 15 °C. The condensation level (cloud base) lies at:
options: 1 000 m — the parcel must cool 10 °C at 1 °C per 100 m

subtopics.title: Clouds — Naming Them and Reading Their Weather

questions.question: In cloud names, 'nimbus' indicates:
options: The cloud is made of ice

questions.question: A thin milky sheet of high cloud producing a halo around the sun or moon is:
Which cloud brings steady, prolonged rain rather than short showers?
A cumulonimbus flattens into an anvil at its top because:
options: The wind blows it sideways at random
It rises until it strikes the tropopause, where the temperature inversion above acts as a ceiling and forces it to spread sideways

questions.question: All three rainfall types share the same four steps. They differ only in:
options: WHAT FORCES THE AIR TO RISE
The season in which they occur

questions.question: The Little Karoo is arid enough for ostrich farming because it:
options: Lies too far north for frontal rain
Sits in the RAIN SHADOW of the Cape mountains — air that has already rained on the seaward slopes descends the leeward side, is compressed, warms, and its relative humidity falls
Is cooled by the Benguela Current

questions.question: The late-afternoon thunderstorm of a Gauteng summer is a textbook example of:
options: CONVECTIONAL rainfall — intense surface heating drives strong thermals that build cumulonimbus, breaking as short, heavy, localised storms

questions.question: The Western Cape's winter rainfall is delivered by:
options: Moist easterly air rising over the Drakensberg
Warm fronts moving in from the north-east
COLD FRONTS sweeping in from the south-west across the Atlantic, one behind another, roughly between May and August

subtopics.title: The Bag That Grows When It's Warm

questions.question: In the shopping-bag picture:
options: Warm air is a BIG bag and cold air is a SMALL bag
Warm air is a small bag and cold air is a big bag
Both bags are the same size
The bag size depends on pressure only

questions.question: A cold Coke sweats on a summer day because:
options: The air touching the cold metal is chilled below its dew point, so its bag shrinks below what it was carrying and the extra comes out as liquid
Salt in the air attracts water

questions.question: The exam habit the section insists on is to:
options: Report the dew point on its own
Report the temperature on its own
Report the GAP between air temperature and dew point — small gap means the bag is nearly full and rain is nearby; big gap means a dry day
Ignore both numbers and read the cloud

subtopics.title: Reading the Sky Like a Menu

questions.question: The four building blocks of cloud names mean:
options: Cirro = high and wispy, alto = middle, strato = spread flat, cumulo = heaped
Cirro = low, alto = high, strato = heaped, cumulo = flat
Cirro = raining, alto = dry, strato = windy, cumulo = still

questions.question: Fog is described as:
options: STRATUS that came all the way down to the ground

questions.question: Fair-weather cumulus clouds all sit on the same invisible shelf because:
options: They are all the same age
That shelf is the CONDENSATION LEVEL — the height at which every parcel in that air mass reaches its dew point

questions.question: Cirrus streaming into the Cape sky in winter usually means:
options: The air is very dry at ground level
A front is roughly a day away — high wispy cloud arrives ahead of the system

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Push Air Up a Hill

questions.question: 'Push number one — the mountain' produces:
options: RELIEF rainfall, wet on the side facing the wind and dry in the rain shadow behind

questions.question: 'Push number two — the hot ground' gives rain that is:
options: Short, violent, loud and very localised — often over your street while the next suburb stays dry

questions.question: 'Push number three — the cold bulldozer' works because:
options: Cold air is lighter and rises
Cold air is heavier, so it shoves underneath the warm air and lifts it right off the ground

questions.question: The examiner's trick the lesson warns about is:
options: Deciding the rainfall type by HOW HARD it is raining instead of by what did the pushing — and then forgetting to name the region and the season, which are separate marks
